title: Edom: The Greatly Despised
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2026-04-18 (date estimated)

Opens [Gen 25](/bible/genesis/25) · [2 Esdras 6](/bible/2-esdras/6) · [Gen 27](/bible/genesis/27) · [Heb 12](/bible/hebrews/12) · [Gen 36](/bible/genesis/36) · [2 Esdras 3](/bible/2-esdras/3) · [Rom 9](/bible/romans/9) · [Mal 1](/bible/malachi/1) · [Obad 1](/bible/obadiah/1) · [Deut 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) · [1 Macc 3](/bible/1-maccabees/3) · [Dan 7](/bible/daniel/7) · [Ps 64](/bible/psalms/64) · [Isa 23](/bible/isaiah/23) · [Ezek 28](/bible/ezekiel/28)
## Introduction Early morning Sabbath class from Captain Abiel, live from San Diego at 9:00 a.m. East Coast time, during the season of Passover while the worldwide blitz covers the four corners of the earth. The class opens with a mini movie built on Obadiah: I have made thee small among the nations, thou art greatly despised; though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, thence will I bring thee down; as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee; but upon Mount Zion shall be deliverance, and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. The question that drives the whole class: who is Esau, how did he become the greatly despised, and why? The class walks from the birth of Jacob and Esau through the birthright and the blessing, then through the receipts of history, decade by decade, asking one question over and over: why is Esau greatly despised? This class is the companion to Captain Zephaniah's class Puerto Rico: The Flame of Resistance, which follows it the same morning. ## Scriptures Opened **[Genesis 25:19-26](/bible/genesis/25#v19)** *[[9:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=567s)]* > [19](/bible/genesis/25#v19) And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham begat Isaac: > > [20](/bible/genesis/25#v20) And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan–aram, the sister to Laban the Syrian. > > [21](/bible/genesis/25#v21) And Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived. > > [22](/bible/genesis/25#v22) And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the Lord. > > [23](/bible/genesis/25#v23) And the Lord said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger. > > [24](/bible/genesis/25#v24) And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb. > > [25](/bible/genesis/25#v25) And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau. > > [26](/bible/genesis/25#v26) And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them. - Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, as all husbands should do: pray for your wives. The Lord was entreated of him, and Rebekah conceived. - The children struggled together within her, and she went to inquire of the Lord. The Lord said unto her: two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels. With that alone you know these children are not the same. They are in the same womb, but they are two different nations. - The one people shall be stronger than the other people: that one people is us, the so-called blacks, Latinos, and Native Americans under the line of Jacob. And the elder shall serve the younger. - The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. The second child is not described, because Jacob was a normal child. Only Rebekah knew the prophecy, because the Lord had told her. **[2 Esdras 6:7-10](/bible/2-esdras/6#v7)** *[[13:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=790s)]* > [7](/bible/2-esdras/6#v7) Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth? > > [8](/bible/2-esdras/6#v8) And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. > > [9](/bible/2-esdras/6#v9) For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. > > [10](/bible/2-esdras/6#v10) The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: other question, Esdras, ask thou not. - Esdras asked, what shall be the parting asunder of the times? When is the end of what we are going through, and the beginning of your kingdom, Lord? - The answer points back to that birth: Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. Esau is the last ruling empire; after Esau gets his run of the blessings, our blessings take place, and they are forever, the everlasting kingdom under Christ. - The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: there is a stretch of things that must go down between Esau's end and the kingdom. And then the angel said, other question, Esdras, ask thou not. **[Genesis 25:27-34](/bible/genesis/25#v27)** *[[15:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=951s)]* > [27](/bible/genesis/25#v27) And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. > > [28](/bible/genesis/25#v28) And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob. > > [29](/bible/genesis/25#v29) And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint: > > [30](/bible/genesis/25#v30) And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom. > > [31](/bible/genesis/25#v31) And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright. > > [32](/bible/genesis/25#v32) And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? > > [33](/bible/genesis/25#v33) And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. > > [34](/bible/genesis/25#v34) Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright. - Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison; but Rebekah loved Jacob, because Rebekah knew what the Lord had told her. - Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage: red pottage with red meat in it, not cooked all the way. Therefore was his name called Edom, which means red.
Reading from *Modern Judaism*, 1830 *[[19:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=1160s)]* > Esau's descendants are the subjects of extensive traditions, in which the rabbis, with effrontery which we should wonder in any other men, have set at defiance all authentic history and an accurate chronology. > First, that the descendants of Esau, sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob, even to the end of the world, - That's us. So, they will never be your friend. To hell with Miss Laura. To hell with Señor Bob. They don't love you. > were at first a small nation inhabiting Mount Seir and the adjacent country. - Mount Seir, I want you to remember that name, Mount Seir. > As long as the Israelites enjoyed a great and formidable empire in Canaan, but that after the powerful republic of the 12 tribes was destroyed by the Assyrians and Babylonians, - Meaning we went into slavery. > they wonderfully increased in number, - I'm talking about Esau. > extended their dominion toward the west, spread their colonies far and wide, subjugated Italy, founded Rome and the Roman Empire, at length entirely overturned the Jewish state which had been restored after the termination of the Babylonian captivity, the second temple being destroyed by Titus Vespasian. > > They hold dominion over all Europe, Esau detaining in captivity his brother Jacob. > Secondly, that the prophecies of the prophets against Esau, Edom, Seir and the cities of Edom, especially those of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Obadiah, have not yet received their full accomplishment, - Meaning that we're in the middle of identifying who these people are. > That this is foretold by the prophets in all their denunciations of the several plagues against the house of Esau, the cities of Edom and Mount Seir, which all belong to Rome and the Christians. - Those are the same people who they hate Jacob, that so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans today. - I'm just reading the highlights cuz I'm limited in time. > But, of the Christians, Obadiah says, "There shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau." - This is future judgment. This is future judgment. We're going to go into that in a moment.
- Esau said, behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? He swore and sold his birthright unto Jacob for bread and pottage of lentils. Thus Esau despised his birthright. It was not taken; he sold it. **[Genesis 27:1-29](/bible/genesis/27#v1)** *[[23:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=1431s)]* > [1](/bible/genesis/27#v1) And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, here am I. > > [2](/bible/genesis/27#v2) And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death: > > [3](/bible/genesis/27#v3) Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison; > > [4](/bible/genesis/27#v4) And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die. > > [5](/bible/genesis/27#v5) And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it. > > [6](/bible/genesis/27#v6) And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying, > > [7](/bible/genesis/27#v7) Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the Lord before my death. > > [8](/bible/genesis/27#v8) Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee. > > [9](/bible/genesis/27#v9) Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth: > > [10](/bible/genesis/27#v10) And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death. > > [11](/bible/genesis/27#v11) And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man: > > [12](/bible/genesis/27#v12) My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing. > > [13](/bible/genesis/27#v13) And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me them. > > [14](/bible/genesis/27#v14) And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved. > > [15](/bible/genesis/27#v15) And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son: > > [16](/bible/genesis/27#v16) And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck: > > [17](/bible/genesis/27#v17) And she gave the savoury meat and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob. > > [18](/bible/genesis/27#v18) And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son? > > [19](/bible/genesis/27#v19) And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me. > > [20](/bible/genesis/27#v20) And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the Lord thy God brought it to me. > > [21](/bible/genesis/27#v21) And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not. > > [22](/bible/genesis/27#v22) And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. > > [23](/bible/genesis/27#v23) And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him. > > [24](/bible/genesis/27#v24) And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am. > > [25](/bible/genesis/27#v25) And he said, Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank. > > [26](/bible/genesis/27#v26) And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son. > > [27](/bible/genesis/27#v27) And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed: > > [28](/bible/genesis/27#v28) Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine: > > [29](/bible/genesis/27#v29) Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. - Isaac, old and dim of sight, asked Esau to take his weapons and bring him savory venison, that my soul may bless thee before I die. Rebekah heard, and commanded Jacob: fetch me two good kids of the goats, and I will make savory meat for thy father. - Christians read this and blame Jacob: he stole Esau's blessing, he lied. No. Esau had already despised and sold his birthright. And Jacob himself objected: Esau is a hairy man, I am a smooth man; my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver, and bring a curse on me. His mother said, upon me be thy curse. Why would she say that? Because she knew the prophecy. She said, this is the moment where the elder shall serve the younger; this is what God told me when the babies were born. I will take the sin; just do what I say. - She put Esau's raiment on Jacob so he would smell like the field, that earthy hunting smell, and the goat skins on his hands and neck. - Isaac is not stupid. How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? Hunting venison takes time: find the tracks, track it, wait. Jacob answered, because the Lord thy God brought it to me. Isaac felt him: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. He asked again, art thou my very son Esau? He ate, he drank, and then, come near now and kiss me, my son, because he wanted to smell him. He smelled the smell of his raiment: yes, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed. - Here the prophecy goes according to what God wanted. How is the elder going to serve the younger if the elder gets all of the blessings? The Lord let Isaac's eyes go dim so he could not discern, and Rebekah put the younger in to receive the elder's blessing: God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine. Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee. Be lord over thy brethren. Cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. - All of us have this blessing, but our blessing does not come into fruition until the appointed time. **[Genesis 27:30-41](/bible/genesis/27#v30)** *[[33:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=2022s)]* > [30](/bible/genesis/27#v30) And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting. > > [31](/bible/genesis/27#v31) And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that thy soul may bless me. > > [32](/bible/genesis/27#v32) And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau. > > [33](/bible/genesis/27#v33) And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed. > > [34](/bible/genesis/27#v34) And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father. > > [35](/bible/genesis/27#v35) And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing. > > [36](/bible/genesis/27#v36) And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me? > > [37](/bible/genesis/27#v37) And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son? > > [38](/bible/genesis/27#v38) And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept. > > [39](/bible/genesis/27#v39) And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; > > [40](/bible/genesis/27#v40) And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck. > > [41](/bible/genesis/27#v41) And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob. - Esau came in from his hunting, and Isaac trembled very exceedingly: who? Where is he that hath taken venison? I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him; yea, and he shall be blessed. Whatever I told that man, he is going to get blessed. - Esau cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry: bless me, even me also, O my father. Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing. Is not he rightly named Jacob? For he hath supplanted me these two times: the birthright, and this moment right here. - Isaac answered: behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants. That is how the elder shall serve the younger. - Then comes the blessing Esau has today: behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above. They would conquer nations and have the best lands, and whatever lands were not in their possession, they would find a way to get them. And by thy sword shalt thou live: Esau, Edom, Idumea lives fighting. And shalt serve thy brother: at the end of everything, the blessing is limited, and it returns to Jacob forever. - And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, when you become the world superpower, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: after you take him out of slavery. - And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing. He said in his heart, the days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob. This is the beginning of the perpetual hatred. **[Hebrews 12:15-17](/bible/hebrews/12#v15)** *[[37:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=2262s)]* > [15](/bible/hebrews/12#v15) Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; > > [16](/bible/hebrews/12#v16) Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. > > [17](/bible/hebrews/12#v17) For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. - How can a man fail of the grace of God? When God says something and you refuse to do it. Esau despised his birthright; that is when you fall from the grace of God. - Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you: Esau became bitter after that, and thereby many were defiled. - Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. When he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He wept before his father, but the deed was already done and the Lord's will was done. **[Genesis 36:1](/bible/genesis/36#v1)** *[[44:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=2676s)]* > [1](/bible/genesis/36#v1) Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom. - Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom. That is all this verse is for: Esau is Edom.
Reading from a web page on Edom *[[44:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=2694s)]* > Edom was an ancient kingdom that stretched across the area in the south of present-day Israel, Jordan, and Palestine. - Ain't that something? Ain't that BS going on over there right now? > Once pushed out of their territories, the … settled during the Persian period in an area comprised in the southern hills of Judea down to the area north of Beersheba. The people appeared under a Greek form of their old name as Idumaeans, and their new territory was called Idumaea, a term used in the Hellenistic and Roman periods, also mentioned in the New Testament. - That right there is called the Treasury, as in Mount Seir. An Edomite stronghold. - That's what we just read in Genesis 27. That's the beginning of Esau's perpetual hatred.
**[2 Esdras 3:12-16](/bible/2-esdras/3#v12)** *[[46:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=2793s)]* > [12](/bible/2-esdras/3#v12) And it happened, that when they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and had gotten them many children, and were a great people, they began again to be more ungodly than the first. > > [13](/bible/2-esdras/3#v13) Now when they lived so wickedly before thee, thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham. > > [14](/bible/2-esdras/3#v14) Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will: > > [15](/bible/2-esdras/3#v15) And madest an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. > > [16](/bible/2-esdras/3#v16) And unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac also thou gavest Jacob and Esau. As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau: and so Jacob became a great multitude. - When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they began again to be more ungodly than the first; they multiplied so heavy that the Most High flooded the earth. - Thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham; him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou showedst thy will, and madest an everlasting covenant with him, promising that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. He was a friend of God. - And unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac also thou gavest Jacob and Esau. As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau: and so Jacob became a great multitude. That is us. God chose Jacob; the younger one is the stronger one, and the elder shall serve him. It was all prophesied. **[Romans 9:9-13](/bible/romans/9#v9)** *[[48:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=2927s)]* > [9](/bible/romans/9#v9) For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son. > > [10](/bible/romans/9#v10) And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; > > [11](/bible/romans/9#v11) (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;) > > [12](/bible/romans/9#v12) It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. > > [13](/bible/romans/9#v13) As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. - The children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil: these babies did nothing wrong; they were in their mother's womb doing nothing but fighting. People ask, how can God just choose like that? Because he is God. He will have mercy on whom he will have mercy. - That the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth. - It was said unto her: not unto him. God told Rebekah how he wanted this thing to go down. The elder shall serve the younger. - As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. It is not of anything good or evil that was done; it is through election. **[Malachi 1:2-4](/bible/malachi/1#v2)** *[[51:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyYFXp99olM&t=3079s)]* > [2](/bible/malachi/1#v2) I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, > > [3](/bible/malachi/1#v3) And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness. > > [4](/bible/malachi/1#v4) Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. - I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, wherein hast thou loved us? That is us right now: police brutality, ICE, what is going on in Sudan, the Jones Act in Puerto Rico and the massacres in Ponce and Utuado, the atrocities in the Congo under Belgium, Shark Island in Namibia, and now the trafficking scandals of our day. How does God love us with all this garbage happening around us? - All these things have to happen, and while they are happening we are supposed to be going to the Lord, repenting, looking in our book, and doing what God says, because the reason we are in these conditions is that we broke God's commandments. - Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste. He is the eldest; he should have had the blessings, but God did not set it up that way. He set it up so we get the blessings forever. That is how he loves us. - Whereas Edom saith, we are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places: they were driven into the mountains, they rebuilt, and now they are the superpower in the world.
